11.ENDOMETRIOSIS:
-Incidence 6 – 10%
-50% among infertile women.

Suspect Endometriosis:

1 or more of the following:

•CPP
•Dysmenorrhea affecting daily activities and QoL
•Dyspareunia (during or after sex)
•Period related/cyclical G.I symptoms.
•Period related/cyclical urinary symptoms:
⇨Dysuria
⇨Hematuria
•Infertility + 1 or more of above.

Assessment:

-Circumstances
-Priorities – cultural/religious belief.
-Fertility desires.
-QOL.

Discuss: - pain and symptoms diary.

Offer: - P/A and P/V examination in all Pts. P/R in rectal disease.

Consider: - USG – TVS

•Even P/A, P/V examination is normal.
•To identify deep endometriosis and endometriomas.

TAS if TVS is not appropriate

MRI:

•Don’t use as 1st line investigation => 1st line only in:
⇨Mullerian anomalies.
⇨CA Cervix – staging.
⇨Before UAE for fibroid mapping.

Diagnostic Laparoscopy:

•Consider laparoscopy in suspected endometriosis even USG is normal.
•Done by Gynecologist skilled/ trained in laparoscopy surgery.
•Take biopsy:
⇨To diagnose (negative biopsy don’t exclude endometriosis).
⇨To rule out malignancy if endometriosis is not excised (1 – 2% risk of Malignancy with endometriosis).
•USG/MRI before laparoscopy if deep endometriosis is suspected.
•Full systematic laparoscopy normal => Explain that there is no endometriosis consider another diagnosis.

Discussion before laparoscopy involves:

•What laparoscopy involves & surgical treatment (with Pt consent).
•Benefits and risks of laparoscopy.
•Effect of laparoscopy on symptoms.
•Need for further surgery that is not planned like deep endometriosis bowel, bladder, ureteric surgery.

Management

Long term support due to significant

Physical mental, social impact.

 

Pain is the issue: Fertility is the Issue:

1st line – 3months - MDT

-Paracetamol

Or

-NSAIDS

Or

-combination

2nd line:

-COC
-progestogens

Neuromodulators:

-PSN
-LUNA

 

 

 

Referral:

Indications:

- NSAID, Paracetamol or

Combination failed.

- Hormonal treatment

not effective

OR not tolerated

OR Contraindicated

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Surgical Management/Laparoscopy:

1.If fertility is a Priority:

Excision/Ablation (depending upon ovarian reserve) ±Adhesiolysis

not in bowel, bladder, ureter

⇨Laparoscopic cystectomy.
⇨Don’t offer hormonal treatment to women who want to conceive.

Incidental lesions:

-Don’t treat.
-Endometria
-<3cm – don’t treat
->3cm – excision

If causing pain or infertility.

Agents used during laparoscopy to reduce Adhesion Formation.

-Oxidized Regenerated cellulose.

-Poly tetra fluoroethylene
-surgical membranes.
-Hyaluronic acid products.

 

2.Fertility is not a priority:
⇨During Diagnostic laparoscopy consider treatment if:
-Peritoneal endometriosis not involving bladder, bowel, ureter.
-Uncomplicated endometriosis (17 – 44% incidence).
⇨Excision:
⇨Deep endometriosis: Bladder, Bowel, Ureters
-Pelvic MRI before OP laparoscopy
-Pretreatment GnRH A 3months.
•Post Treatment => Hormonal suppression
•GnRH A avoided in adolescent as they have not reached Max BMD.
•Letrozole in deep endometriosis or nodules that are not respectable.

 

 

Hysterectomy:

•Excise all visible endometriotic lesions @ the time of TAH.
•Decision by MDT.

 

Sub Fertility Management’s

Operative Laparoscopy
Stage I & II (ASF, ASRM):

⇨Operative laparoscopy
-Adhesiolysis
-Excision
-Ablation
⇨prefer Co2 laser over coagulation
⇨Higher pregnancy with laser

Stage III & IV:

⇨Operative laparoscopy
-Remove endometriosis.
-Adhesiolysis
⇨Laparoscopy improve fertility outcome.

Menopause & HRT in endometriosis:

⇨Combined HRT.
⇨Tibolone only with GnRH A.

USG appearance of Endometriosis:

⇨Ground glass appearance.
⇨1 – 4 compartments.
⇨No papillary structure with presence of blood flow.

IUI Stage I & II

•IUI rather expectant
•Stimulated rather unstimulated
•Within 6m` of surgery.

IVF:

-Male factor
-Tubal factor
-Failed treatment

Pre Treatment:

- with GnRH A for 3 – 6m` before IVF in all endometriosis Pts improve fertility outcome.

Surgery before IVF:

-Mild disease = Adhesiolysis
-Severe, dense Adhesions or frozen pelvis => No Adhesiolysis just salpingectomy.

Indications for pre-Treatment surgery:

1.To improve access
2.To relief pain.

Antibiotic Prophylaxis:

-Before egg retrieval in presence of Endometriosis.
